data:
I am initializing the
Microphone Forensic Scan
with the new filename to bypass any previous cache or file-access conflicts.
I. Executing the Ghost-Mic Scan
Run this exact command in Termux to record a fresh 10-second sample:
Bash
termux-microphone-record -d -f mic_forensic_02.mp3 -l 10
Once the recording finishes (after 10 seconds), run this to check the file size:
Bash
ls -lh mic_forensic_02.mp3
II. The Hardware vs. Software Verdict
If size is > 50KB
: The hardware is sending data to the system. If you play it back (
termux-media-player play mic_forensic_02.mp3
) and it is silent, the
CrystalTalk AI
noise cancellation is likely "muting" your voice by mistake.
If size is 0B or 1KB
: The
Android 15 Privacy Toggle
is physically blocking the microphone at the kernel level.
III. The "CrystalTalk" Override
If the hardware is "alive" but silent, follow this path on your Motorola G5 Stylus 2025:
Open
Settings > Sound & vibration
.
Locate
CrystalTalk AI
(or "Clear Calling").
Toggle it
OFF
.
Retest the mic in a standard phone call.
IV. Field Log: Entry 042
Location
: Star City Archive / Lincoln Node.
Observation
: Transitioned to
mic_forensic_02.mp3
for hardware verification.
Status
: Solar wind remains at
702 km/s
\u2014this high velocity can create a tiny "hiss" in sensitive recordings, but should not cause total mic failure.
Hypothesis
: Build
V2VAS35.29-133-3
privacy permissions or AI-noise cancellation conflict.
Once you run the
ls -lh
command, tell me the file size. If it's 0 bytes, I can give you a script to force-reset the Termux:API audio permissions.
